newsitem.title: USA: Ill. official seeks Mercury Finance hearing.
newsitem.headline: Ill. official seeks Mercury Finance hearing.

text.p: Illinois Treasurer Judy Baar Topinka on Friday called for legislative hearings into local government investment practices in the wake of school district holdings of debt issued by troubled Mercury Finance Co.

Topinka said she has received calls from state lawmakers interested in working with her office to tighten state investment laws which she said allow local governments to invest public funds in speculative instruments.

Topinka's call for hearings was spurred by news reports that school investment funds run by Cadre Financial Services Inc, a unit of AMBAC Inc, had invested in commercial paper of Mercury Finance, a Lake Forest, Ill., consumer finance company that said last week it was in default on its short-term lending agreements.
AMBAC said Friday that Cadre had sold all holdings of Mercury Finance commercial paper at no loss to two state funds it runs in Illinois and Michigan.
"AMBAC can say everything is fine because they're claiming to bail out (the Illinois fund)," Topinka said. "But how many AMBACs are there going to be?"
AMBAC said the commercial paper sale would have no impact on its earnings. A spokesman for the bond insurer declined to say if the paper was sold at a loss and if so who absorbed that loss.
Topinka said she wants to keep Illinois investment laws tight to avoid situations like the one faced by Orange County, Calif., which filed for bankruptcy protection in December 1994.
"Before thinking in terms of expanding investments in unsecured assets, we need to take a look at where we're going," she said.
